message.content:
**Answer:**  
One of the most celebrated and instantly recognisable sculptures created in the 19th century is **“The Thinker” by Auguste Rodin**, originally conceived as part of his monumental project *Gates of Hell* (completed between 1902‑1917). Although it was finished at the very end of the century, its conception began in the late 1800s, and it quickly captured public imagination—its contemplative pose and expressive musculature have made it emblematic of modern art and philosophy alike.  

Other contemporaneous masterpieces include:

| Artist | Sculpture | Year |
|--------|-----------|------|
| Antonio Canova | “Cupid and Psyche” | 1795–1819 |
| Jean-Baptiste Carpeaux | “The Dance” (Paris Opera Ballet) | 1861 |
| Gutzon Borglum | “Statue of Abraham Lincoln” (Washington D.C.) | 1878 |

These works collectively illustrate how the 19th century shifted toward realism, romanticism, and eventually impressionistic approaches within sculpture.
